findings.title: The strip_prefix-plus-lossy "path relative to root" idiom is written four times in the plugin crate
findings.problem: Four copies of one three-line reduction, under three different names (`display_rel`, `rel_to_repo`, and inlined at the tail of `rel_to_state`). Two of them share a name across modules while one of the same-named pair is spelled with `.unwrap_or(path)` instead of `.unwrap_or_else(|_| …)`; a reader grepping `display_rel` finds two definitions and cannot tell whether they agree.
findings.proposal: Add one `pub(crate) fn display_rel(root: &Path, path: &Path) -> String` to the plugin crate's existing path-helper module `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/pathnorm.rs` (it already owns the crate's lexical path helpers and is imported by the gate modules). Have `hook/session_start.rs`, `hook/pre_compact.rs` (renaming `rel_to_repo` away entirely) and `checklist/verbs.rs` call it, and have `hook/subagent_stop.rs::rel_to_state` keep its state-root derivation but end in `pathnorm::display_rel(root, path)`.
findings.behavior_preservation: All four bodies compute the same string: `strip_prefix` returns `Ok(rel)` or `Err(StripPrefixError)`, and the checklist variant's `.unwrap_or(path)` yields the same `path` the other variant's `.unwrap_or_else(|_| …)` falls back to; `to_string_lossy().into_owned()` is then applied to the identical `Path` in every case. No caller inspects the error, so the outputs, the absence of I/O and the call ordering are unchanged.

findings.title: STATE_QUERY is defined twice as the same hardcoded literal while a third site derives it from core's STATE_REL
findings.problem: The one path core owns (`ss_magic_core::state_tree::STATE_REL`, re-exported as `scratchpad::STATE_REL`) is re-spelled as a slash-suffixed literal in two private consts with the same name and near-identical doc comments, while `status.rs` derives the very same value from `STATE_REL`. Three spellings of one query string, two of which are independent literals that a change to `STATE_REL` would silently leave behind.
findings.proposal: Keep exactly one definition: make `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/scratchpad.rs:66`'s const `pub(crate) const STATE_QUERY: &str = ".superset/.magic/";` (it already re-exports `STATE_REL` and owns the state tree), delete `hook/mod.rs:93` and import `crate::scratchpad::STATE_QUERY` there, and replace `status.rs:1270`'s `format!` with the same const.
findings.behavior_preservation: All three sites currently evaluate to the byte-identical string `".superset/.magic/"` (`STATE_REL` is `.superset/.magic`, so the `format!` appends the same slash), and each is passed to `git::is_ignored_no_index_str` or interpolated into a message. Substituting one const for three equal values changes no argument, message or ordering; `status.rs` loses one heap allocation per call and nothing else.

findings.title: The ignored-state-tree probe and its two refusal sentences are written twice, word for word apart from one suffix
findings.problem: Two modules independently spell the same fail-closed probe and the same two sentences; `hook/mod.rs`'s versions differ only by a trailing `. No state was written.` on each. A wording fix in one leaves the other stale, and the heartbeat row and the guidance block would then disagree about the same refusal.
findings.proposal: Add `pub(crate) fn ignore_refusal(root: &Path) -> Option<String>` to `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/scratchpad.rs`, holding the probe and the two base sentences exactly as `scratchpad` spells them today (no trailing suffix). `scratchpad::ensure` uses its result as `Refusal::NotIgnored { detail }`; `hook/mod.rs::state_tree_refusal` becomes `scratchpad::ignore_refusal(root).map(|base| format!("{base}. No state was written."))`. Both call sites keep their own probe call, so neither gate is thinned or skipped.
findings.behavior_preservation: The suffixed strings reproduce today's `hook/mod.rs` text exactly (`"… to add it"` + `". No state was written."` = `"… to add it. No state was written."`; `"… is ignored: {e}"` + `". No state was written."` = today's error sentence), and the `Ok(true) => None` / fail-closed `Err` mapping is unchanged. Each caller still performs its own `git::is_ignored_no_index_str` call at the same point in its flow, so the number and ordering of subprocesses is untouched.

findings.title: Every state-writing hook runs the same `git check-ignore --no-index` probe twice per invocation
findings.problem: The pipeline gate asks git whether `.superset/.magic/` is ignored, and the handler it then dispatches to immediately calls `scratchpad::ensure`, whose first act is the identical `git::is_ignored_no_index_str(root, STATE_QUERY)` probe. That is two `git` process spawns per `SessionStart`, `PreCompact` and `SubagentStop` invocation for one question already answered — on `SessionEnd`'s budget-sensitive sibling events, and on a path the module doc describes as the cost every invocation pays.
findings.proposal: Carry the verdict rather than dropping it: have `hook/mod.rs::gate_and_dispatch` record the `Ok(true)` it already obtained on `HookContext` (a new `state_tree_ignored: bool` field beside `main_root`), and add `pub(crate) fn ensure_verified(cwd: &Path) -> Result<Report>` to `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/scratchpad.rs` that skips only the ignore probe and is callable only with that flag set; the three hook handlers call it, and the public `ensure` — used by `status`, the verbs and every non-hook caller — keeps probing exactly as now.
findings.behavior_preservation: The skipped probe is the same call against the same root, made microseconds earlier in the same process, and it is only skipped when it returned `Ok(true)` (the gate returns before dispatch on `Ok(false)` and on `Err`). The `Report` a handler receives is otherwise built identically, so refusals, guidance text and heartbeat details are unchanged. Marked as touching a safety check because it moves a fail-closed probe's result across a call boundary; if the reviewer judges the flag too easy to mis-set later, the finding should be dropped rather than weakened.

findings.title: SessionStart reads the plugin pin file twice, from two notices that document themselves as reading one pin
findings.evidence:
session_start.rs:331   let pinned = read_pin(plugin_root)?;            // version_drift_notice
session_start.rs:394   let pinned = read_pin(surroundings.plugin_root.as_deref());   // release_suggestion
session_start.rs:347   /// … Shared by
session_start.rs:348   /// the version-drift notice and the release suggestion so the two can never
session_start.rs:349   /// read a different pin.
findings.problem: `read_pin` is a file read (`status::read_pin_file`), and both notices call it on every `startup`. The doc comment claims the two "can never read a different pin", but they read the file twice and could in principle disagree; the sharing is only of the function, not of the value.
findings.proposal: In `handle_with`, read it once — `let pinned = read_pin(surroundings.plugin_root.as_deref());` — and pass `pinned.as_deref()` into `version_drift_notice` and `release_suggestion`, changing both signatures to take the already-read pin instead of a `plugin_root`.
findings.behavior_preservation: `version_drift_notice` already reads the pin unconditionally on every source, so hoisting the read never adds one: a non-`startup` session still performs exactly one read (release_suggestion returns at its `source != "startup"` check before reaching the pin today, and would simply be handed a value it ignores), and a `startup` goes from two reads to one. The value is identical in both because the file is not written between the two calls, and the notices' texts and ordering are unchanged.

findings.title: The cache-directory closure is invoked twice per SessionStart, and each call runs create_dir_all
findings.problem: On a `startup` where the compaction advice reaches its marker step, `compaction_advice` and `release_suggestion` each invoke the injected `cache_dir` closure, and the production closure is `release::cache_dir`, which resolves `ProjectDirs` and calls `create_dir_all` every time. The second resolution and mkdir are pure repeat work on the session-start path.
findings.proposal: Memoize inside `handle_with` without losing the laziness the `Surroundings` doc requires: build a local `let cached = std::cell::OnceCell::new();` and a closure `|| cached.get_or_init(|| (surroundings.cache_dir)()).clone()`, and pass that closure to both `compaction_advice` and `release_suggestion` in place of the raw one.
findings.behavior_preservation: The closure is still called only when a branch actually needs the directory, so a plain `resume` — or a startup without the override — still never touches the cache directory, which is the property the doc pins. When it is needed, `release::cache_dir` is idempotent (`create_dir_all` on an existing directory is `Ok`), so one call returns the same `Option<PathBuf>` the second call would have; every marker path, cache path and heartbeat detail is unchanged.

findings.title: pre_compact computes the same `trigger_display` fallback twice in one file
findings.evidence:
pre_compact.rs:82    let trigger_display = if trigger.is_empty() { "(unset)" } else { trigger };
pre_compact.rs:189   let trigger_display = if trigger.is_empty() { "(unset)" } else { trigger };
findings.problem: `handle` renders the trigger for the heartbeat detail and `append_note` renders it again for the file body, from the same input, with the same literal `"(unset)"` spelled twice. The two are required to agree (the row and the note describe one event) but nothing makes them.
findings.proposal: Add one private `fn trigger_display(trigger: &str) -> &str { if trigger.is_empty() { "(unset)" } else { trigger } }` to `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/hook/pre_compact.rs` and call it from both sites, so the `"(unset)"` literal exists once.
findings.behavior_preservation: Both call sites are already the identical expression over the identical `trigger` value (`append_note` receives the same `&str` `handle` matched out of the payload), so extracting it yields byte-identical output in the heartbeat detail and in the note's `## <ts> — trigger: …` line.

findings.title: Three handlers repeat the same repo_root guard and the same hard-coded detail sentence
findings.problem: The same heartbeat sentence is a bare string literal in three handlers, each preceded by a four-line comment restating the same `HookContext::repo_root` contract. The heartbeat vocabulary is otherwise centralised as named `REASON_*` consts in `hook/mod.rs`; this one class of note is stringly-typed and triplicated instead.
findings.proposal: Add `pub(crate) const NO_REPOSITORY_DETAIL: &str = "not inside a git repository; nothing to do";` next to the `REASON_*` block in `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/hook/mod.rs` and use it at all three sites (keeping each handler's own `let Some(repo_root) = … else` / `if ctx.repo_root.is_none()` shape, which differs because two of them need the bound root).
findings.behavior_preservation: Only a literal is replaced by a const holding that literal; the guards, their position in each handler and every emitted `Outcome` stay identical.

findings.title: `pre_compact::is_tracked` is a narrower copy of `subagent_stop::tracked_under`, and collides by name with `scratchpad::is_tracked`
findings.problem: Two hook handlers each carry their own scan of `Report::refusals` for a tracked path, differing only by the `rel/` prefix branch, and the narrower one is named `is_tracked` — the same name `scratchpad` uses for an unrelated question ("does git report this tracked", against a live `HashSet`). A reader grepping the name gets two different answers, and a fix to the refusal scan has two homes.
findings.proposal: Move `tracked_under(report: &Report, rel: &str) -> bool` up to `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/hook/mod.rs` as `pub(super) fn tracked_under`, and have both `hook/pre_compact.rs` and `hook/subagent_stop.rs` call it — deleting `pre_compact::is_tracked` and with it the name clash.
findings.behavior_preservation: For the file path `pre_compact` passes (`<session dir>/PRE-COMPACT.md`), `tracked_under`'s extra `p.starts_with("<rel>/")` arm can only match if git tracks a path *inside* something named `PRE-COMPACT.md`, i.e. if that name is a directory — in which case today's code proceeds to open it and fails with an I/O error, while the shared helper refuses quietly. Every other input is answered identically. The divergence is only in that impossible-in-practice case and moves the handler further toward its own fail-closed posture, so confidence is 75 rather than 100.

findings.title: The owner-only file mode is nine private FILE_MODE consts, one inline literal in this partition, and one same-named const holding a different value
findings.problem: `const FILE_MODE: u32 = 0o600` exists nine times in the plugin crate (`bypass`, `cache`, `expect_artifact`, `heartbeat`, `ledger`, `scratchpad`, `hook/file_changed`, `hook/subagent_stop`, `hook/pre_compact`), `setup_ci.rs` binds the SAME name to `0o644`, and this partition also writes the mode as a bare `0o600` literal in `session_start::claim_marker` — so the crate has three spellings of one policy and one name that means two different things.
findings.proposal: Declare `pub(crate) const OWNER_ONLY_MODE: u32 = 0o600;` once (beside `write_atomically` in `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/atomic.rs`, which already takes a mode parameter and is the crate's shared write primitive), have the nine 0o600 sites and `session_start.rs:301`'s inline literal use it, and rename `setup_ci.rs`'s const to `COMMITTED_FILE_MODE` so no two values share a name.
findings.behavior_preservation: Every replaced site passes the same `u32` to the same `OpenOptionsExt::mode` / `set_permissions` call, so the on-disk modes are unchanged; the `setup_ci` rename touches a private const with a single reader. `pre_compact.rs`'s doc comment defending the local copy is superseded by the shared const and should be rewritten rather than deleted.

findings.title: The `unroutable-event` heartbeat class has two independent owners
findings.problem: One string names one condition, but it is spelled independently in a bare const in `hook/mod.rs` (used by the pre-decode screen) and in `DecodeError::class`'s match arm (used when the same condition is reached through `decode`). `class()` is documented as "a stable, machine-readable class … so changing the human text below never breaks anything reading the log" — yet the log's other producer of that class is not tied to it.
findings.proposal: Own it once in `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/hook/event.rs`: `pub(crate) const CLASS_UNROUTABLE: &str = "unroutable-event";`, returned by `DecodeError::class`'s `Unroutable` arm, and referenced from `hook/mod.rs` in place of `REASON_UNROUTABLE` (or as its initializer, keeping the local name).
findings.behavior_preservation: The emitted class string is the same literal on both paths, so every heartbeat row, `status` count and grep over the log is byte-identical.

findings.title: STATE_FILE_NOTES retypes the six state-file names that scratchpad::STATE_FILES already owns
findings.evidence:
session_start.rs:66  /// `(file name, one-line description)`, in the exact order and spelling of
session_start.rs:67  /// [`scratchpad::STATE_FILES`]. … a name here that U8 does not actually create
session_start.rs:68  const STATE_FILE_NOTES: [(&str, &str); 6] = [ ("CONTEXT.md", …), ("DECISIONS.md", …), …
scratchpad.rs:80     pub const STATE_FILES: [&str; 6] = [ "CONTEXT.md", "DECISIONS.md", … ];
findings.problem: The six names are typed a second time purely so a description can sit beside each, and the const's own doc comment says a name that diverges would be "guidance worse than none". The divergence is currently caught only at test time (`state_file_notes_match_what_u8_actually_scaffolds`), i.e. by a test that exists to police a duplication rather than a behavior.
findings.proposal: Replace the pair array with `const STATE_FILE_DESCRIPTIONS: [&str; scratchpad::STATE_FILES.len()]` holding only the six descriptions in the same order, and render with `for (name, desc) in scratchpad::STATE_FILES.iter().zip(STATE_FILE_DESCRIPTIONS)` at `session_start.rs:549`. The array-length expression makes a future seventh state file a compile error instead of a test failure.
findings.behavior_preservation: The names and their order are byte-identical between the two arrays today (verified item by item), so the rendered `{name:<22}{desc}` lines — and therefore the whole `additionalContext` body — are unchanged.

findings.title: The harness's 10,000-character additionalContext cliff is spelled as a bare number in four comments and one test assertion
findings.evidence:
event.rs:357          /// cliffs at 10,000 characters and is replaced by a persisted-output preview
event.rs:397          /// model at all. Budget `additional_context` under 10,000 characters or
session_start.rs:464  /// this one line past R19's 10,000-character budget on every session start,
pre_tool_use.rs:1554  /// 10,000-character cliff (`hook/event.rs`), so unlike the Read gate's cached
tests.rs:261          text.len() < 10_000,
findings.problem: One measured harness limit is restated as a literal in four doc comments across three modules and asserted as a bare `10_000` in a test, while a differently-purposed `GATE_INLINE_BYTE_BUDGET_DEFAULT: u32 = 10_000` lives in `config.rs` for the Read gate's inline budget. Nothing ties the four sites together, and the coincidence of the two numbers invites a reader to assume one governs the other.
findings.proposal: Declare the limit once where the wire format is owned — `pub(crate) const ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT_CLIFF_CHARS: usize = 10_000;` in `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/hook/event.rs`, documented as the measured harness cliff — reference it by name from the three other doc comments, and use it in `session_start/tests.rs:261`'s assertion in place of the literal.
findings.behavior_preservation: Nothing but a test literal is replaced by a const of the same value; the four comment sites are prose. `config.rs`'s `GATE_INLINE_BYTE_BUDGET_DEFAULT` is deliberately left alone — it is a configurable, clamped default for a different channel and must not be aliased to this const.

findings.title: Four comments in hook/mod.rs still describe a pre-U12 state in which the handlers had not landed
findings.evidence:
mod.rs:182  // The pipeline builds every field; the readers are the per-event handlers of
mod.rs:183  // U12 onward, so until those land the compiler sees write-only fields.
mod.rs:229  // Read by the per-event handlers of U12 onward; the tests here already
mod.rs:238  // First production caller arrives with the per-event handlers; exercised by
mod.rs:265  // Used by the per-event handlers as they land; the stubs below return
mod.rs:266  // `silent`.
findings.problem: All six handlers have landed, `HookContext::cwd` is read by three of them, `Outcome::new` is constructed by `session_start`, and there are no stubs left in this module — so these four comments narrate task history that no longer describes the code. Two of them also mis-state the present: `cwd()` is not waiting for a reader, and `Outcome::new`'s "the stubs below" has no referent.
findings.proposal: Delete the four narration comments. Where they carry a live fact, restate it as one: on `HookContext::event` and `main_root` keep the existing doc comment's reason for the `#[allow(dead_code)]` (the field records which root the gate read `enabled` from) and drop the U12 sentence; on `diagnostic`, replace the note with "no handler writes a diagnostic today; the channel exists so one can, without touching stderr itself".
findings.behavior_preservation: Comment-only edits; no expression, attribute or signature changes.

findings.title: `base` names two different row builders in one function, and a third identical closure is redeclared in the next
findings.problem: Inside `pipeline`, `base()` means "a row with no cwd" above line 458 and "a row carrying the envelope's cwd" below it — a shadow that changes what the same call produces halfway down the function, in code whose whole subject is what a heartbeat row records. `gate_and_dispatch` then re-declares the identical second closure a third time.
findings.proposal: Rename the first closure to `bare_row` (its two callers are the unroutable branch at 430 and the `NoInput` branch at 445, both of which deliberately have no decoded cwd), and pass the second closure's row builder down rather than redeclaring it: give `gate_and_dispatch` the already-built `base` closure as a parameter, or drop both closures and call `base_row(event, &envelope.common.cwd, now)` directly at each of its use sites.
findings.behavior_preservation: Renaming a local closure and either reusing or inlining an identical one changes no constructed `Row`: `base_row` is a pure function of `(event, cwd, now)`, all three of which are fixed for the invocation.

nothing_to_flag: Rubric 1 item 2 (standard-library or runtime primitives): no hand-rolled loop in this partition has a behavior-equivalent std replacement; `join_system_messages`, `panic_message` and `from_raw` are each already the thinnest form of what they do.

Rubric 1 item 3 (platform/framework guarantees): nothing here hand-maintains a guarantee serde, the harness or the kernel already provides; the `create_new` exclusivity in `pre_compact::append_note` and `session_start::claim_marker` is the correct use of the kernel's guarantee, not a re-implementation.
Rubric 2 item 1 (redundant state): no cached value in this partition duplicates derivable state beyond the repeated reads already reported as F5/F6.

Rubric 2 item 2 (parameter sprawl): `Surroundings`, `HookIo` and the injected `route`/`now` are documented testability seams (structure-pins: "Testability seams that inject the environment … are not parameter sprawl").
Rubric 2 item 6 (unnecessary wrapper elements): not applicable — no component-tree UI framework here.
Rubric 2 item 7 (nested conditionals): nothing in this partition nests three or more levels; the deepest is the two-level match in `release_suggestion`.

Rubric 2 item 9 (dead code): `HookContext::event`, `HookContext::main_root` and `HookContext::diagnostic` are unread in production but each carries a documented reason and an `#[allow(dead_code)]`; only their stale narration is reported (F14), not their removal.

Rubric 2 item 10 (context-dependent vocabulary): the R-numbers and U-numbers in doc comments are the repository's own established vocabulary and are paired with prose explanations, per the repo's comment convention.

Rubric 2 item 11 (pre-release compatibility scaffolding): `hook/file_changed.rs`'s routing is deliberately kept exercised though the manifest declares no such event (CLAUDE.md); `FileChanged::file_paths` tolerates a spelling the harness never sends, also deliberate.

Rubric 3 item 2 (missed concurrency): the pipeline's git probe, config resolution and handler dispatch are ordered dependencies; the one detachable piece (the release refresh) is already spawned detached.
Rubric 3 item 4 (recurring no-op updates): no polling or reducer surface in this partition.
Rubric 3 item 6 (memory): every buffer here is bounded — stdin is one envelope, diagnostics are handler-produced lines, and the heartbeat's own pruning lives outside this partition.
Rubric 3 item 7 (overly broad operations): the only whole-file reads are the pin file and the release cache, both small and both already single-purpose.

Test helpers: `ignored_repo()` is byte-identical in `hook/session_start/tests.rs:28`, `hook/pre_compact/tests.rs:28` and `hook/subagent_stop/tests.rs:32`, but `ss_magic_core::testutil` provides no equivalent (only `init_main_repo`), so per the brief's rule this is not reported as a finding.
